summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis, steroid dependence, and multiple comorbidities was admitted for hypotension and recurrent falls following a reduction in prednisone dose. He presented with systolic blood pressure as low as 70, requiring vasopressor support and ICU admission. Evaluation revealed acute kidney injury likely due to hypovolemia, negative head and neck imaging after trauma from falls, and no evidence of sepsis or acute cardiac event. Adrenal insufficiency was considered a contributing factor. He was treated with stress-dose hydrocortisone, fluid resuscitation, and vasopressors, which were successfully weaned. His blood pressure stabilized, renal function improved, and he was transitioned to 10 mg daily oral prednisone with a rescue dexamethasone dose for home use. Other medications were adjusted, including reduction of carvedilol and temporary hold of spironolactone, with torsemide restarted at 50 mg daily. He developed a diarrhea episode consistent with IBS, which resolved with supportive care. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans across multiple specialties.
problems: Diabetes with ophthalmic manifestations, type II or unspecified type, uncontrolled
